cracks.title: Cracks
cracks.cause: Your kidney filter value (eGFR) is lower than normal, so waste is not cleared as well.
cracks.tip: Take medicines as your doctor says and avoid pain-killers like ibuprofen.

leak.title: Leaking drops
leak.cause: Protein is leaking into your urine. This means the kidney filters are damaged.
leak.tip: Controlling blood pressure and sugar reduces the leak. Ask your doctor about a protective medicine.

veins.title: Swollen veins
veins.cause: High blood pressure is straining your kidneys.
veins.tip: Eat less salt, take your blood pressure medicine daily, and check your pressure at home.

pallor.title: Pale colour
pallor.cause: Your haemoglobin is low (anaemia). Damaged kidneys make less of the hormone that builds blood.
pallor.tip: Tell your doctor. Do not self-medicate with iron or tonics.

flicker.title: Flickering pulse
flicker.cause: Your potassium is high. This can upset the heart rhythm.
flicker.tip: Limit bananas, coconut water and potatoes, and contact your doctor soon.

carePlan.title: My care plan
carePlan.intro: Simple steps for healthier kidneys. Medicines are decided only by your doctor.

sections.warning_signs: Go to a doctor if you notice

items.urgent_stage5: Your kidney function is in the kidney-failure range. Please contact your doctor or the nearest hospital today.
items.urgent_potassium: Your potassium is very high ({{potassium}}). This can affect the heart. Please contact a doctor today.
items.urgent_bp: Your blood pressure is very high ({{sbp}}). Please contact a doctor today.
items.diet_salt: Keep salt low: under 5 g of salt (about 1 teaspoon) a day. Avoid pickles, papad, salted snacks, instant noodles and salted fish.
items.diet_protein: Do not eat extra protein. About 0.8 g of protein per kg of body weight per day is usual; your doctor or dietitian will tell you the right amount.
items.diet_potassium_high: Your potassium is high ({{potassium}}). Limit bananas, tender coconut water, potatoes, tomatoes and leafy-green curries until your doctor says otherwise.
items.diet_phosphate: Limit processed foods, colas and packaged snacks (hidden phosphate). Ask your doctor about phosphate tests.
items.fluids_general: Drink water normally unless your doctor has asked you to limit fluids. Do not drink large amounts to 'flush' the kidneys.
items.fluids_ask: In advanced kidney disease your doctor may set a daily fluid limit. Ask at your next visit.
items.bp_target: Check your blood pressure regularly. A usual goal for people with CKD is below 130/80; your doctor will set your target.
items.sugar_target: Keep blood sugar controlled. HbA1c around 7% is a common goal; your doctor will set yours.
items.avoid_nsaids: Do not take pain-killers such as ibuprofen, diclofenac or naproxen. They can harm the kidneys. Ask a doctor or pharmacist for a safe alternative.
items.avoid_herbal: Tell your doctor about all herbal, ayurvedic or traditional medicines. Some can harm the kidneys.
items.sick_day: If you have vomiting or diarrhoea, call your doctor: some medicines may need to be paused for a short time.
items.activity_walk: Walk or do light exercise most days (about 150 minutes a week) as your doctor allows.
items.no_tobacco: Do not smoke or chew tobacco.
items.monitor_frequency: You should have kidney blood and urine tests about {{per_year}} time(s) a year.
items.monitor_home: Write down your blood pressure and weight. Bring all reports to each visit.
items.warn_swelling: Go to a doctor urgently if you have swelling of the feet, legs or face.
items.warn_breath: Go to a doctor urgently if you have breathlessness.
items.warn_urine: Go to a doctor urgently if you pass much less urine than usual.
items.warn_vomit: Go to a doctor urgently if you have continuous vomiting or severe weakness.
items.warn_chest: Go to a doctor urgently if you have chest pain or a very slow or irregular heartbeat.

glossary.egfr: eGFR: how well your kidneys filter blood. Higher is better.
glossary.creatinine: Creatinine: a waste product in the blood. It rises when kidneys filter less.
glossary.albuminuria: Albuminuria: protein leaking into the urine, a sign of kidney damage.
glossary.potassium: Potassium: a mineral. Too much can upset the heart rhythm.
glossary.dialysis: Dialysis: a treatment that cleans the blood when the kidneys fail.
glossary.ckd: CKD: chronic kidney disease, a slow loss of kidney function.

journey.headIn: {{label}}: your eGFR is already in the kidney-failure range (below 15). Please stay under a kidney specialist's care.
journey.headMost: {{label}}: kidney failure range (eGFR below 15) is most likely around {{year}} (age {{age}}), between {{from}} and {{to}}.
journey.headNot: {{label}}: kidney failure is not expected in the next {{n}} years ({{p}}% chance).
journey.subtitle: Your kidney journey: how fast it may change, when the big steps may come, and where people like you end up. Estimates, not promises.
journey.whenTitle: When could the kidney reach failure range?
journey.gain: These changes could add about {{n}} years before kidney failure range.
journey.ownTrend: Your own {{n}} lab results show your eGFR changing by {{v}} per year. That trend is part of the forecast.
journey.leversBody: Tick the changes you want to test. Effects are typical trial ranges, shown as estimates. Your doctor decides what is right for you.
journey.notNeeded: does not apply to your current numbers
journey.chartBody: The shaded band holds 8 of 10 simulated futures with today's care. Lines show the middle path. Below 15 is kidney failure range.
journey.sliderLine: Blue line: the year chosen on the slider
journey.milestonesTitle: Milestones: when and at what age
journey.milestonesBody: Median year with the age you will be, and the range from a fast to a slow decline.
journey.txNote: Transplant evaluation window (eGFR about 20) and dialysis start (often eGFR 5 to 10, or when symptoms appear) are typical guidance; your doctor decides the timing.
journey.atYear: What this stage is usually like
journey.outTitle: Where people like you end up
journey.outBody: Imagine 100 people with the same age, labs and health as you. This shows how many would be doing well, in kidney failure range, or would have died, year by year. It is a group picture, not a prediction for one person.
journey.outNote: Dialysis or a transplant is not modelled. They change what happens after kidney failure range, so use this as a reason to plan early, not as a verdict.
journey.survTitle: Out of 100 people like you, how many are alive
journey.survBody: From a survival model fitted on thousands of US adults. It describes groups, never one person, and it cannot say what will happen to you.
journey.planNote: Dates use the faster end of the range (1 in 10 futures) so that planning starts early enough.
journey.how1: We simulate 2,500 possible futures. Each starts from your latest eGFR and a yearly decline drawn from your own lab trend (when you have 3 or more results) blended with typical rates for people with your urine protein, blood pressure, diabetes and age.
journey.how2: Every future is checked against the milestones above. Where people end up uses a survival model that also looks at each future's own kidney function year by year.
journey.leverHow_bp_control: Sets systolic BP to 125 if it is higher
journey.leverHow_sugar_control: Sets HbA1c to 7.0 if it is higher
journey.lever_protein_drug: ACE inhibitor / ARB for urine protein
journey.leverHow_protein_drug: Lowers urine ACR by about 35% (typical range 30-40%)
journey.leverHow_sglt2: Slows the excess decline by about 30% (trials: roughly 30-40%)
